name: Dogfood 042: Multi-phase workflow — Go daemon (RFC 0039 Phase 1) + Engram RFC 0044 + Repo-local-PG RFC 0042

native_delegation.instruction: Use native delegation aggressively for parallelizable work. The parent session remains accountable for Striatum artifacts, write scope, verification, and completion. This is a one-shot supervised invocation: you cannot ask the operator a follow-up question. If a step is ambiguous, choose the most-conservative default that matches the synthesis and proceed; the operator publishes the result on your behalf if your CLI access is denied. For long-running test runs, prefer focused pytest invocations before the wider `make test` to avoid lease expiry beyond ~30 minutes.

Use sub-agents aggressively for bounded independent research, review, and code/test/doc authorship. This is a one-shot supervised invocation: you cannot ask the operator a follow-up question. If permission to call `striatum ack` is denied, write the artifact and exit normally; the operator publishes on your behalf.

Use local sub-agents only for bounded independent work. This is a one-shot supervised invocation: write the artifact in this single call; do not surface strategy and exit without producing the file. When writing finding artifacts, ALL FIVE front-matter fields are required (none are optional): schema_version, artifact_kind, verdict_intent, severity, tags. Use schema_version: "striatum.finding.v1" exactly (not "1"); verdict_intent (not verdict); severity from {low,medium,high,critical} (not none); tags as a JSON array; the `author:` byline is a plain markdown line AFTER the front-matter block. Handoff artifacts (DESIGN.md / HANDOFF.md / RFC bodies) do not need front matter; just the plain `author:` byline.

command: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m striatum.cli skills install --profile all --scope user --force --json >/dev/null && export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" && exec .striatum/bin/codex-supervised-wrapper.sh
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m striatum.cli skills install --profile all --scope user --force --json >/dev/null && export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" && exec .striatum/bin/claude-supervised-wrapper.sh
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m striatum.cli skills install --profile all --scope user --force --json >/dev/null && export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" && exec .striatum/bin/gemini-supervised-wrapper.sh

jobs.title: Track A design: Go daemon (codex)
jobs.objective: Produce implementation design for RFC 0039 Phase 1 Steps 1+2 only (Go skeleton + envelope-v1 + Postgres substrate). Cover go/ layout, RPC server, capability table, audit chain reuse, Postgres connection + migration loader. Do NOT design Steps 3-6 yet; those land in Phase 2 of this multi-phase workflow.

jobs.title: Track A design: Go daemon (claude)
jobs.objective: Produce implementation design for RFC 0039 Phase 1 Steps 1+2 emphasizing trust boundaries (Go subprocess + Python CLI + Postgres) and operator-mistake footguns. Cover Go subprocess lifecycle, signal handling, PTY, packaging.

jobs.title: Track A design: Go daemon (gemini)
jobs.objective: Produce implementation design for RFC 0039 Phase 1 Steps 1+2 with attention to cross-platform reality (Linux + macOS only, no Windows daemon), supply-chain considerations for Go module dependencies, audit-chain integrity across the SQL layer.

jobs.title: Track A synthesis: Go daemon
jobs.objective: Synthesize 3 Go daemon designs into one plan for Steps 1+2. Pick concrete Go layout, RPC envelope-v1 implementation, capability table, audit chain reuse, Postgres connection + migration loader. Defer Steps 3-6 to Phase 2.

jobs.title: Track A design review: Go daemon (threat_model)
jobs.objective: Review the Go daemon Steps 1+2 synthesis under threat_model posture. Capability table correctness, audit chain integrity, subprocess trust boundary, Postgres credential handling.

jobs.title: Track A implement: Go core (codex)
jobs.objective: Implement Steps 1+2 Go-side: `go/cmd/striatumd/`, `go/pkg/rpc/{envelope,registry,capability,server}.go`, `go/pkg/db/{connection,migrations,audit}.go`, `go/go.mod`, `go/Makefile`. Daemon at this stage handles read-only RPC verbs only. Reads same migrations from `src/striatum/daemon_pg/sql/*.sql` (or embedded). Use sub-agents aggressively.

jobs.title: Track A implement: Python glue + harness extension + docs (claude)
jobs.objective: Implement Steps 1+2 Python-side: extend RFC 0035 multi-repo harness with `daemon_core` parameter (`tests/_harness/multi_repo.py`); extend `tests/_harness/daemon.py` to optionally launch the Go binary; docs updates (HOW_TO_HUMAN section on Go daemon, SPEC daemon section, CHANGELOG, RFC 0039 status block). Do NOT yet add `--core go` CLI flag (that's Phase 2).

jobs.title: Track A build review (codex, threat_model)
jobs.objective: Review Go daemon Steps 1+2 build under threat_model posture. Focus on Go systems angle: envelope-v1 correctness, capability authorization, audit chain helper reuse, Postgres connection security.

jobs.title: Track A build review (claude, threat_model)
jobs.objective: Review Go daemon Steps 1+2 under threat_model posture. Focus on the Python-side integration: harness extension correctness, docs honesty, Python ↔ Go subprocess trust boundary.

jobs.title: Track A build review (gemini, adversarial)
jobs.objective: Review Go daemon Steps 1+2 under threat_model posture from the adversarial angle. Focus on: Go module supply-chain hygiene (go.sum verification, no unverified deps), cross-platform reality (builds same on Linux + macOS), audit chain tamper attempts, PG credential leakage paths, env var injection.

jobs.title: Track B design: Engram Phase 1 RFC (codex)
jobs.objective: Produce design for RFC 0044 (Engram Phase 1: read-only Engram MCP server over Striatum corpus). MUST read all .md files under ~/git/engram/ before proposing. Augment Engram's existing mission; do not redesign. Output is a design for an RFC body, not the RFC itself.

jobs.title: Track B design: Engram Phase 1 RFC (claude)
jobs.objective: Produce design for RFC 0044 emphasizing the operator UX: how the Striatum-side operator session discovers + queries the Engram MCP server. MUST read all .md files under ~/git/engram/ before proposing. Read RFC 0041 (which scopes the design phase) carefully.

jobs.title: Track B design: Engram Phase 1 RFC (gemini)
jobs.objective: Produce design for RFC 0044 with attention to cross-corpus separation, capability tokens scoped to Striatum corpus only, Engram unavailability fallback (Striatum must run without Engram). MUST read all .md files under ~/git/engram/ before proposing.

jobs.title: Track B synthesis: Engram Phase 1 RFC plan
jobs.objective: Synthesize 3 Engram designs into one plan for RFC 0044 V1 acceptance criteria. Cite specific Engram concepts (claims, beliefs, ingestion, segmentation) accurately from ~/git/engram/ docs.

jobs.title: Track B design review: Engram (ergonomics_dx)
jobs.objective: Review Engram RFC 0044 synthesis under ergonomics_dx posture. Verify the design augments Engram's existing mission (does not replace), preserves Engram's claims/beliefs schemas, and the read-only retrieval path is discoverable to a first-time operator.

jobs.title: Track B implement: Draft RFC 0044 (codex)
jobs.objective: Write RFC 0044 body (Engram Phase 1 implementation spec) from the synthesis. Acceptance-criteria-bearing RFC; concrete enough that a future dogfood can implement against it. Do NOT update docs/rfcs/README.md or docs/TODO.md (the consolidate_phase_1 job does that).

jobs.title: Track B build review: RFC 0044 (codex, ergonomics_dx)
jobs.objective: Review RFC 0044 body under ergonomics_dx posture. Focus on technical clarity: schema choices, MCP capability vocabulary, retrieval API shape, augmentation-not-replacement boundary preserved.

jobs.title: Track B build review: RFC 0044 (claude, ergonomics_dx)
jobs.objective: Review RFC 0044 body under ergonomics_dx posture. Focus on operator-side UX: how a first-time operator discovers + uses the Engram retrieval surface, augmentation boundary clear, graceful degradation on Engram unavailability.

jobs.title: Track B build review: RFC 0044 (gemini, ergonomics_dx)
jobs.objective: Review RFC 0044 body under ergonomics_dx posture from adversarial angle. Focus on: Engram fluency (does the RFC accurately cite Engram's existing schemas from ~/git/engram/), claim provenance honesty, capability scope between corpora, what cannot be claimed.

jobs.title: Track C design: Repo-local PG migration (codex)
jobs.objective: Produce design for RFC 0042 V1: move repo-local state (.striatum/state.sqlite3 schemas — runs, jobs, sessions, leases, queue, events, etc.) into the daemon's Postgres DB, keyed by repo_id. Single-user trust boundary stays (D083). Multi-tenancy = schema-level per-repo isolation. Cover migration verb (striatum daemon migrate-repo-local --from sqlite --to pg), .striatum/ → operational scratch only.

jobs.title: Track C design: Repo-local PG migration (claude)
jobs.objective: Produce design for RFC 0042 V1 emphasizing trust boundaries (daemon mandatory; CLI behavior when no daemon running — refuse cleanly with named remediation, not silent fallback). Per-repo-id keying; new schemas; how RFC 0039 Go daemon scope expands to be gateway for ALL repo-local ops from day 1.

jobs.title: Track C design: Repo-local PG migration (gemini)
jobs.objective: Produce design for RFC 0042 V1 with attention to: migration story (preserve SQLite copy read-only as rollback), schema changes (add repo_id to every repo-local table), concurrent operators on one machine (single-tenant trust per D083; no auth changes), failure modes (daemon down, PG unavailable, partial migration).

jobs.title: Track C synthesis: RFC 0042 plan
jobs.objective: Synthesize 3 PG designs into one plan for RFC 0042 V1 acceptance criteria. Concrete schema changes, migration verb spec, RFC 0039 scope revision, CLI behavior without daemon, D006/D007/D028 supersession framing.

jobs.title: Track C design review: PG migration (threat_model)
jobs.objective: Review RFC 0042 synthesis under threat_model posture. Migration safety (rollback path), schema integrity, audit chain integrity preserved across migration, daemon-mandatory boundary defensible.

jobs.title: Track C implement: Draft RFC 0042 (codex)
jobs.objective: Write RFC 0042 body (repo-local state to Postgres) from the synthesis. Includes: schema changes, migration verb spec, RFC 0039 scope revision, CLI behavior without daemon, D006/D007/D028 supersession. Do NOT update docs/rfcs/README.md (consolidate_phase_1 does that). Reference D093 (encoded in parallel session) for the decision-log entry.

jobs.title: Track C build review: RFC 0042 (codex, threat_model)
jobs.objective: Review RFC 0042 body under threat_model posture. Migration safety, schema integrity, daemon-mandatory boundary, audit chain preservation.

jobs.title: Track C build review: RFC 0042 (claude, threat_model)
jobs.objective: Review RFC 0042 body under threat_model posture. CLI behavior when daemon unavailable, RFC 0039 scope revision correctness, supersession of D006/D007/D028 written cleanly.

jobs.title: Track C build review: RFC 0042 (gemini, adversarial)
jobs.objective: Review RFC 0042 body under threat_model posture from adversarial angle. Concurrent operators (single-tenant trust per D083), failure modes (PG unavailable mid-write), audit chain tamper across migration, rollback safety.

jobs.title: Consolidation: Phase 1 cross-cutting updates
jobs.objective: After all three tracks complete: update docs/rfcs/README.md (add RFC 0042 + RFC 0044 entries; bump RFC 0039 status if appropriate), docs/TODO.md (mark progress on items 21+), CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entries for each landed track, BUILD_HANDOFF.md for Phase 1 covering all three tracks. Write the Phase 1 OPERATOR_REPORT.md.
